## Per-finding outcome (all 11 verified from disk, not from the notes)

**Confirmed, fix genuinely on disk:** B1-1, B2-1, B2-3, B2-4, B2-5, B2-7, B3-1, B3-2, B3-3. No Beta pushed back on anything, so there was no pushback to adjudicate; B3-2 is the mirror case — my own decline of Beta-3's F2, which Beta-3 accepted and whose stale text it replaced with the disk fact.

**B2-2 — applied, and correct in substance, but the fix introduced two defects I repaired:**

1. **Out-of-closure dependency (blocking).** The corollary added by the B2-7 fix, `cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five`, cited `lem-direct-product-of-finite-cyclic-groups-is-cyclic-iff-orders-are-coprime` — published on `primitive-roots-and-unit-groups-modulo-n` at **order 57.001**, in neither the manifest's nor the plan's `requires` closure for page 70. Same class as B3-1/B2-4, arriving inside the repair of a different one, and invisible to `content-policy` and `coverage-checklist` because the id resolves. Repaired to the in-closure route `thm-order-of-element-in-direct-product` + `thm-classification-of-cyclic-groups` (lcm(5,21)=105), in the manifest deps, the strategy and contract step 4.1.
2. **A title asserting what the page cannot prove.** `ex-sylow-subgroups-of-gl-two-over-a-finite-prime-field` was titled `Sylow p-subgroups of Aut((Z/p)²) ≅ GL_2(F_p)` — but the entire point of the fix is that `GL_2(F_p)` is undefined until order 78. That is B2-1's defect (a Statement claiming more than the proof gives) reappearing in B2-2's repair, and it is invisible to the judges. Title corrected; the conventional name kept as an explicit name-only Remark instruction in both strategies, and the `coverage.json` note that claimed the item "proves the coordinate dictionary" corrected to what it actually does.

I verified the rebuilt mathematics rather than accepting it: the Heisenberg coordinate law and diagonal action are exactly the unipotent/torus conjugation of the matrix group, `|B_p| = p³(p−1)³`; the new `|Aut((Z/p)²)| = (p²−1)(p²−p)` theorem and its `n_p = p+1` consequence close, including that normalising the shear subgroup is equivalent to preserving its fixed line.

**B2-6 — confirmed with a recorded limitation.** I downloaded Judson and read it: printed p. 220 = PDF p. 227, Theorems 13.1–13.3 and the stopping point are exactly as the locator claims. The range is only three pages, so I read pp. 222–228 too, to check what that costs — **nothing standard is lost**; Sylow II/III come from Conrad, which I verified verbatim at step 3. Textbook backing is now present but supporting, not primary.
